findings.body: The new _memory override raises whenever an active job sees blocked_by, and legacy.ACTIVE includes draining. In the actual inherited Shared45Controller.tick, both memory calls precede completion of child.poll/owned-drain finalization. If unrelated external usage keeps capacity blocked, every draining tick throws before polling an already-exited owned leader. Owned pidfd signals continue, but the genuine leader wait, job drain record and controller close cannot progress until unrelated external capacity recovers. This makes the proposed persistent-capacity failstop unable to complete its required owned drain independently of external jobs.
findings.reproduction: The independent checker compiles only the exact new factory and extracted unchanged Shared0 _memory plus Shared45 tick/_fail_owned_supervision/_service_termination against handwritten RAM doubles. On an 80GiB fake GPU with preserved external50GiB and a30GiB H058 reservation+4GiB headroom, an already-exited child receives zero poll calls over three draining ticks while signal-service counters advance1,3,5. It remains in children throughout. Only after external capacity becomes clear does the next tick poll once, finalize the failed job and close.
findings.required_repair: Preserve the active capacity predicate and owned-only abort, but route the capacity violation into recorded resource-abort/draining state without throwing ahead of mandatory leader polling, adopted waits and terminal drain checks. Add a RAM-only inherited-tick test where the capacity blocker persists after the owned child exits, and prove leader wait/drain/close finish while external usage remains unchanged. No production failure probe is needed.
